name: Copenhagen Burnout Inventory
developer: Kristensen, Borritz, Villadsen and Christensen (2005), National Research Centre for the Working Environment, Denmark
construct: Burnout as fatigue and exhaustion attributed to three domains: life in general, work, and work with clients.
licence: NFA (National Research Centre for the Working Environment): the CBI "may be used freely for non-commercial and commercial purposes, provided that the following source is clearly cited" (Borritz et al., 2006, Scandinavian Journal of Public Health). The first edition PDF itself carries no copyright statement.

subscales.name: Personal burnout
subscales.description: "Personal burnout is a state of prolonged physical and psychological exhaustion." Scale is valid if at least 3 of 6 items answered.

subscales.name: Work related burnout
subscales.description: "Work burnout is a state of prolonged physical and psychological exhaustion, which is perceived as related to the person's work." Item 13 reversed. Scale is valid if at least 4 of 7 items answered.

subscales.name: Client related burnout
subscales.description: "Client burnout is a state of prolonged physical and psychological exhaustion, which is perceived as related to the person's work with clients." Scale is valid if at least 3 of 6 items answered. The word clients is replaced by the relevant term (patients, students, inmates and so on).

scoring: Score each response Always or To a very high degree = 100, Often or To a high degree = 75, Sometimes or Somewhat = 50, Seldom or To a low degree = 25, Never/almost never or To a very low degree = 0, with item 13 reversed. Each subscale score is the mean of its items (0 to 100); higher scores indicate more burnout. A respondent is treated as a non responder on a scale if fewer than 3 personal items, fewer than 4 work items or fewer than 3 client items are answered. The NFA source gives no formal cut off; the PUMA study treated 50 or more as high burnout, and later studies commonly use 50 to 74 moderate, 75 to 99 high and 100 severe. The source recommends not presenting items in the order printed and mixing them with items on other topics.
citation: Kristensen, T. S., Borritz, M., Villadsen, E., & Christensen, K. B. (2005). The Copenhagen Burnout Inventory: A new tool for the assessment of burnout. Work & Stress, 19(3), 192–207. https://doi.org/10.1080/02678370500297720
transcriptionNote: Items transcribed from the NFA first edition PDF (Borritz and Kristensen, February 2004). The PDF prints the items grouped by scale without consecutive numbering; numbers 1 to 19 here follow the printed order (personal, work, client). The PDF gives no respondent instructions, only the 3 scale definitions quoted in the subscale descriptions. The PDF lists numeric values (100, 75, 50, 25, 0) only for the frequency scale and says the degree scale is scored "as for the first scale", so the same values are applied to the degree labels. Each item's response scale type is given in its note field because the two scales are used for different items. Second pass: item 4 quotation characters corrected to the PDF.
